newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA fines corporate finance firm 40,000 stg.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA fines corporate finance firm 40,000 stg.

text.p: UK financial markets regulator the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Tuesday it had reprimanded and fined corporate finance and investment management firm English Trust Company Ltd.

The SFA said the 40,000 stg fine and an order to pay costs were for "failings relating to underwriting an offer and placing on the Unlisted Securities Market". The chairman and an executive director have been reprimanded, fined and ordered to pay costs.

The SFA said in a statement it had severely reprimanded Stephen Goschalk, a director of English Trust specialising in corporate finance, as well as fining him 10,000 stg. He has also agreed to pay costs of 3,200 stg.
Christopher Spence, English Trust's chairman and senior executive officer, was reprimanded, fined 5,000 stg and has agreed to pay costs of 3,200 stg.
The SFA said it had begun proceedings against the company and the two individuals in September 1996 and all three had co-operated fully with it in the course of its investigations.
In a statement the SFA said English Trust had agreed to underwrite an offer and placing for a USM quoted company in January 1995.

English Trust agreed to accept two separate firms as sub-underwriters and placees but made inadequate checks into the ability of the two to finance the transactions "and in the event they both defaulted on their sub-underwriting and placing commitments".

In attempting to get the deal to go-ahead, English Trust and its client entered into an agreement whereby others agreed to take up the shortfall and as part of this English Trust agreed to sell shares to a company, the SFA said.

But English Trust "failed to exercise sufficient due diligence in relation to its ability to meet a commitment to purchase shares and was content to rely on assurances given by this company's chief executive, notwithstanding the existence of grounds for questioning his reliability," it added.
This company failed to pay for the shares by the agreed settlement date, although it eventually settled nearly two months after the original payment deadline.

The SFA said it had taken into account the fact that English Trust. Goschalk and Spence had relied in good faith on the "veracity of representations made by the chairman of the client company and other representatives of the defaulting companies".
It also recognised that English Trust "eventually received and remitted to the client company all amounts due in respect of the offer and placing".
